title: अंश ४ · अध्याय ६

items.text: (सोमवंशवर्णनम्)
items.tr: (somavaṃśavarṇanam)

items.speaker: मैत्रेय उवाच
items.text:
सूर्यस्य वंश्या भगवन् कथिता भवता मम ।
सोमस्याप्यखिलान् वंश्याञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि पार्थिवान् ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
sūryasya vaṃśyā bhagavan kathitā bhavatā mama |
somasyāpyakhilān vaṃśyāñchrotumicchāmi pārthivān || 1 ||

items.text:
कीर्त्यते स्थिरकीर्तीनां येषामद्यापि सन्ततिः ।
प्रसादसुमुखस्तान् मे ब्रह्मन्नाख्यातुमर्हसि ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
kīrtyate sthirakīrtīnāṃ yeṣāmadyāpi santatiḥ |
prasādasumukhastān me brahmannākhyātumarhasi || 2 ||

items.speaker: पराशर उवाच
items.text:
श्रूयतां मुनिशार्दूल वंशः प्रथिततेजसः ।
सोमस्यानुक्रमात् ख्याता यत्रोर्वीपतयोऽभवन् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
śrūyatāṃ muniśārdūla vaṃśaḥ prathitatejasaḥ |
somasyānukramāt khyātā yatrorvīpatayo'bhavan || 3 ||

items.text: अयं हि वंशः अतिबल-पराक्रम-द्युति-शील-चेष्टावद्भिः अतिगुणान्वितैः नहुष-ययाति-कार्तवीर्यार्जुनादिभिः भूपालैः अलङ्कृतः तमहं कथयामि श्रूयताम् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr: ayaṃ hi vaṃśaḥ atibala-parākrama-dyuti-śīla-ceṣṭāvadbhiḥ atiguṇānvitaiḥ nahuṣa-yayāti-kārtavīryārjunādibhiḥ bhūpālaiḥ alaṅkṛtaḥ tamahaṃ kathayāmi śrūyatām || 4 ||

items.text: अखिलजगत्स्रष्टुर्भगवतो नारायणस्य नाभिसरोजसमुद्भवाब्जयोनेर्ब्रह्मणः पुत्रोऽत्रिः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr: akhilajagatsraṣṭurbhagavato nārāyaṇasya nābhisarojasamudbhavābjayonerbrahmaṇaḥ putro'triḥ || 5 ||
atreḥ somaḥ || 6 ||

items.text: तं च भगवान् अब्जयोनिः अशेषौषधीद्विजनक्षत्राणाम् आधिपत्ये अभ्यषेचयत् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr: taṃ ca bhagavān abjayoniḥ aśeṣauṣadhīdvijanakṣatrāṇām ādhipatye abhyaṣecayat || 7 ||

items.text: स च राजसूयमकरोत् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr: sa ca rājasūyamakarot || 8 ||

items.text: तत्प्रभावात् अत्युत्कृष्टाधिपत्याधिष्ठातृत्वात् च एनं मद आविवेश ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr: tatprabhāvāt atyutkṛṣṭādhipatyādhiṣṭhātṛtvāt ca enaṃ mada āviveśa || 9 ||

items.text: मदावलेपाच्च सकलदेवगुरोः बृस्पतेः तारां नाम पत्नीं जहार ॥ १० ॥
items.tr: madāvalepācca sakaladevaguroḥ bṛspateḥ tārāṃ nāma patnīṃ jahāra || 10 ||

items.text: बहुशश्च बृहस्पतिचोदितेन भगवता ब्रह्मणा चोद्यमानः सकलैश्च देवर्षिभिः याच्यमानोऽपि न मुमोच ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr: bahuśaśca bṛhaspaticoditena bhagavatā brahmaṇā codyamānaḥ sakalaiśca devarṣibhiḥ yācyamāno'pi na mumoca || 11 ||

items.text: तस्य चन्द्रस्य च बृहस्पतेः द्वेषात् उशना पार्ष्णिग्राहः अभूत् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr: tasya candrasya ca bṛhaspateḥ dveṣāt uśanā pārṣṇigrāhaḥ abhūt || 12 ||

items.text: अङ्गिरसश्च सकाशात् उपलब्धविद्यो भगवान् रुद्रो बृहस्पतेः सहाय्यमकरोत् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr: aṅgirasaśca sakāśāt upalabdhavidyo bhagavān rudro bṛhaspateḥ sahāyyamakarot || 13 ||

items.text: यतश्चोशना ततो जम्भकुम्भाद्याः समस्ता एव दैत्यदानवनिकाया महान्तमुद्यमं चक्रुः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr: yataścośanā tato jambhakumbhādyāḥ samastā eva daityadānavanikāyā mahāntamudyamaṃ cakruḥ || 14 ||

items.text: बृहस्पतेरपि सकलदेवसैन्ययुतः सहायः शक्रोऽभवत् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr: bṛhaspaterapi sakaladevasainyayutaḥ sahāyaḥ śakro'bhavat || 15 ||

items.text: एवं च तयोः अतीव उग्रसंग्रामः तारानिमित्तः तारकामयो नामाभूत् ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr: evaṃ ca tayoḥ atīva ugrasaṃgrāmaḥ tārānimittaḥ tārakāmayo nāmābhūt || 16 ||

items.text: ततश्च समस्तशस्त्राणि असुरेषु रुद्रपुरोगमा देवा, देवेषु च अशेषदानवा मुमुचुः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr: tataśca samastaśastrāṇi asureṣu rudrapurogamā devā, deveṣu ca aśeṣadānavā mumucuḥ || 17 ||

items.text: एवं देवासुराहवसंक्षोभक्षुब्धहृदयम् अशेषमेव जगत् ब्रह्माणं शरणं जगाम ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr: evaṃ devāsurāhavasaṃkṣobhakṣubdhahṛdayam aśeṣameva jagat brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagāma || 18 ||

items.text: ततश्च भगवान् अब्जयोनिः अपि उशनसं शङ्करम् असुरान् देवांश्च निवार्य, बृहस्पतये ताराम् अदापयत् ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr: tataśca bhagavān abjayoniḥ api uśanasaṃ śaṅkaram asurān devāṃśca nivārya, bṛhaspataye tārām adāpayat || 19 ||

items.text: तां च अन्तःप्रसवाम् अवलोक्य बृहस्पतिरपि आह ॥ २० ॥
items.tr: tāṃ ca antaḥprasavām avalokya bṛhaspatirapi āha || 20 ||

items.text: “नैष मम, क्षेत्रे भवत्या अन्यस्य सुतो धार्यः, समुत्सृज एनम्, अलमलम् अतिधार्ष्ट्येन” इति ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr: “naiṣa mama, kṣetre bhavatyā anyasya suto dhāryaḥ, samutsṛja enam, alamalam atidhārṣṭyena” iti || 21 ||

items.text: सा च तेन एवम् उक्ता अतिपतिव्रता भर्तृवचनानन्तरं तम् इषीकास्तम्बे गर्भम् उत्ससर्ज ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr: sā ca tena evam uktā atipativratā bhartṛvacanānantaraṃ tam iṣīkāstambe garbham utsasarja || 22 ||

items.text: स च उत्सृष्टमात्र एव अतितेजसा देवानां तेजांसि आचिक्षेप ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr: sa ca utsṛṣṭamātra eva atitejasā devānāṃ tejāṃsi ācikṣepa || 23 ||

items.text: बृहस्पतिम् इन्दुं च तस्य कुमारस्य अतिचारुतया साभिलाषौ दृष्ट्वा, देवाः समुत्पन्नसन्देहाः तारां पप्रच्छुः ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr: bṛhaspatim induṃ ca tasya kumārasya aticārutayā sābhilāṣau dṛṣṭvā, devāḥ samutpannasandehāḥ tārāṃ papracchuḥ || 24 ||

items.text: “सत्यं कथय अस्माकम् इति सुभगे सोमस्य, अथ वा बृहस्पतेः अयं पुत्र” इति ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr: “satyaṃ kathaya asmākam iti subhage somasya, atha vā bṛhaspateḥ ayaṃ putra” iti || 25 ||

items.text: एवं तैरुक्ता सा तारा ह्रिया किञ्चिन्नोवाच ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr: evaṃ tairuktā sā tārā hriyā kiñcinnovāca || 26 ||

items.text: बहुशोऽप्यभिहिता यदासौ देवेभ्यो नाचचक्षे, ततः स कुमारः तां शप्तुम् उद्यतः प्राह ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr: bahuśo'pyabhihitā yadāsau devebhyo nācacakṣe, tataḥ sa kumāraḥ tāṃ śaptum udyataḥ prāha || 27 ||

items.text: “दुष्टेऽम्ब कस्मान्मम तातं नाख्यासि ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr: “duṣṭe'mba kasmānmama tātaṃ nākhyāsi || 28 ||

items.text: अद्यैव ते व्यलीकलज्जावत्याः तथा शास्तिम् अहं करोमि ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr: adyaiva te vyalīkalajjāvatyāḥ tathā śāstim ahaṃ karomi || 29 ||

items.text: यथा च नैवम् अद्यापि अतिमन्थरवचना भविष्यसि” इति ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr: yathā ca naivam adyāpi atimantharavacanā bhaviṣyasi” iti || 30 ||

items.text: अथ भगवान् पितामहः तं कुमारं सन्निवार्य स्वयमपृच्छत् तां ताराम् ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr: atha bhagavān pitāmahaḥ taṃ kumāraṃ sannivārya svayamapṛcchat tāṃ tārām || 31 ||

items.text: “कथय वत्से कस्यायमात्मजः सोमस्य वा बृहस्पतेर्वा” इत्युक्ता लज्जमानाह “सोमस्य” इति ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr: “kathaya vatse kasyāyamātmajaḥ somasya vā bṛhaspatervā” ityuktā lajjamānāha “somasya” iti || 32 ||

items.text: ततः प्रस्फुरद्-उच्छ्वासित-अमल-कपोल-कान्तिः भगवान् उडुपतिः कुमारमालिङ्ग्य “साधु साधु वत्स प्राज्ञोऽसि” इति ‘बुध’ इति तस्य च नाम चक्रे ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr: tataḥ prasphurad-ucchvāsita-amala-kapola-kāntiḥ bhagavān uḍupatiḥ kumāramāliṅgya “sādhu sādhu vatsa prājño'si” iti ‘budha’ iti tasya ca nāma cakre || 33 ||

items.text: तदाख्यातमेवैतत्, स च यथा इलायाम् आत्मजं पुरूरवसम् उत्पादयामास ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr: tadākhyātamevaitat, sa ca yathā ilāyām ātmajaṃ purūravasam utpādayāmāsa || 34 ||

items.text: पुरूरवास्तु अतिदानशीलोऽतियज्वा अतितेजस्वी । यं सत्यवादिनम् अतिरूपवन्तं मनस्विनं “मित्रावरुणशापात् मानुषे लोके मया वस्तव्यम्” इति कृतमतिः ऊर्वशी ददर्श ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr: purūravāstu atidānaśīlo'tiyajvā atitejasvī | yaṃ satyavādinam atirūpavantaṃ manasvinaṃ “mitrāvaruṇaśāpāt mānuṣe loke mayā vastavyam” iti kṛtamatiḥ ūrvaśī dadarśa || 35 ||

items.text: दृष्टमात्रे च तस्मिन् अपहाय मानमशेषमपास्य स्वर्गसुखाभिलाषं तन्मनस्का भूत्वा तमेव उपतस्थे ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr: dṛṣṭamātre ca tasmin apahāya mānamaśeṣamapāsya svargasukhābhilāṣaṃ tanmanaskā bhūtvā tameva upatasthe || 36 ||

items.text: सोऽपि च ताम् अतिशयित-सकल-लोक-स्त्री-कान्ति-सौकुमार्य-लावण्य-गति-विलास-हासादि-गुणाम् अवलोक्य तदायत्तचित्तवृत्तिः बभूव ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr: so'pi ca tām atiśayita-sakala-loka-strī-kānti-saukumārya-lāvaṇya-gati-vilāsa-hāsādi-guṇām avalokya tadāyattacittavṛttiḥ babhūva || 37 ||

items.text: उभयमपि तन्मनस्कम् अनन्यदृष्टि परित्यक्तसमस्तान्यप्रयोजनम् अभूत् ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr: ubhayamapi tanmanaskam ananyadṛṣṭi parityaktasamastānyaprayojanam abhūt || 38 ||

items.text: राजा तु प्रागल्भ्यात् तामाह ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr: rājā tu prāgalbhyāt tāmāha || 39 ||

items.text: “सुभ्रु त्वामहमभिकामोऽस्मि, प्रसीद अनुरागमुद्वह” इत्युक्ता लज्जावखण्डितम् उर्वशी तं प्राह ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr: “subhru tvāmahamabhikāmo'smi, prasīda anurāgamudvaha” ityuktā lajjāvakhaṇḍitam urvaśī taṃ prāha || 40 ||

items.text: “भवत्वेवं यदि मे समयपरिपालनं भवान् करोति” इत्याख्याते पुनरपि तामाह ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr: “bhavatvevaṃ yadi me samayaparipālanaṃ bhavān karoti” ityākhyāte punarapi tāmāha || 41 ||

items.text: “आख्याहि मे समयम्” इति ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr: “ākhyāhi me samayam” iti || 42 ||

items.text: अथ पृष्टा पुनरप्यब्रवीत् ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr: atha pṛṣṭā punarapyabravīt || 43 ||

items.text: “शयनसमीपे ममोरणकद्वयं पुत्रभूतं नापनेयम् ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr: “śayanasamīpe mamoraṇakadvayaṃ putrabhūtaṃ nāpaneyam || 44 ||

items.text: भवांश्च मया न नग्नो द्रष्टव्यः ॥ ४५ ॥
items.tr: bhavāṃśca mayā na nagno draṣṭavyaḥ || 45 ||

items.text: घृतमात्रं च ममाहार” इति ॥ ४६ ॥
items.tr: ghṛtamātraṃ ca mamāhāra” iti || 46 ||

items.text: “एवमेव” इति भूपतिरप्याह ॥ ४७ ॥
items.tr: “evameva” iti bhūpatirapyāha || 47 ||

items.text: तया सह स चावनिपतिरलकायां चैत्ररथादिवनेषु अमलपद्मखण्डेषु मानसादिसरस्सु अतिरमणीयेषु रममाणः, षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि अनुदिनप्रवर्धमानप्रमोदः अनयत् ॥ ४८ ॥
items.tr: tayā saha sa cāvanipatiralakāyāṃ caitrarathādivaneṣu amalapadmakhaṇḍeṣu mānasādisarassu atiramaṇīyeṣu ramamāṇaḥ, ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi anudinapravardhamānapramodaḥ anayat || 48 ||

items.text: उर्वशी च तदुपभोगात् प्रतिदिनप्रवर्धमानानुरागा अमरलोकवासेऽपि न स्पृहां चकार ॥ ४९ ॥
items.tr: urvaśī ca tadupabhogāt pratidinapravardhamānānurāgā amaralokavāse'pi na spṛhāṃ cakāra || 49 ||

items.text: विना चोर्वश्या सुरलोकोऽप्सरसां सिद्धगन्धर्वाणां च नातिरमणीयोऽभवत् ॥ ५० ॥
items.tr: vinā corvaśyā suraloko'psarasāṃ siddhagandharvāṇāṃ ca nātiramaṇīyo'bhavat || 50 ||

items.text: ततश्चोर्वशीपुरूरवसोः समयविद्विश्वावसुः गन्धर्वसमवेतो निशि शयनाभ्याशात् एकमुरणकं जहार ॥ ५१ ॥
items.tr: tataścorvaśīpurūravasoḥ samayavidviśvāvasuḥ gandharvasamaveto niśi śayanābhyāśāt ekamuraṇakaṃ jahāra || 51 ||

items.text: तस्याकाशे नीयमानस्योर्वशी शब्दमशृणोत् ॥ ५२ ॥
items.tr: tasyākāśe nīyamānasyorvaśī śabdamaśṛṇot || 52 ||

items.text: एवमुवाच च “ममानाथायाः पुत्रः केनापह्रियते, कं शरणमुपयामि” इति ॥ ५३ ॥
items.tr: evamuvāca ca “mamānāthāyāḥ putraḥ kenāpahriyate, kaṃ śaraṇamupayāmi” iti || 53 ||

items.text: तदाकर्ण्य राजा “मां नग्नं देवी वीक्ष्यति” इति न ययौ ॥ ५४ ॥
items.tr: tadākarṇya rājā “māṃ nagnaṃ devī vīkṣyati” iti na yayau || 54 ||

items.text: अथ अन्यमपि उरणकम् आदाय गन्धर्वा ययुः ॥ ५५ ॥
items.tr: atha anyamapi uraṇakam ādāya gandharvā yayuḥ || 55 ||

items.text: तस्यापि अपह्रियमाणस्य आकर्ण्य शब्दमाकाशे पुनरपि “अनाथास्मि अहम् अभर्तृका कापुरुषाश्रया” इत्यार्तराविणी बभूव ॥ ५६ ॥
items.tr: tasyāpi apahriyamāṇasya ākarṇya śabdamākāśe punarapi “anāthāsmi aham abhartṛkā kāpuruṣāśrayā” ityārtarāviṇī babhūva || 56 ||

items.text: राजापि अमर्षवशात् अन्धकारमेतदिति खड्गमादाय “दुष्ट दुष्ट हतोऽसि” इति व्याहरन् अभ्यधावत् ॥ ५७ ॥
items.tr: rājāpi amarṣavaśāt andhakārametaditi khaḍgamādāya “duṣṭa duṣṭa hato'si” iti vyāharan abhyadhāvat || 57 ||

items.text: तावच्च गन्धर्वैरपि अतीवोज्ज्वला विद्युज्जनिता ॥ ५८ ॥
items.tr: tāvacca gandharvairapi atīvojjvalā vidyujjanitā || 58 ||

items.text: तत्प्रभया चोर्वशी राजानम् अपगताम्बरं दृष्ट्वा अपवृत्तसमया तत्क्षणादेव अपक्रान्ता ॥ ५९ ॥
items.tr: tatprabhayā corvaśī rājānam apagatāmbaraṃ dṛṣṭvā apavṛttasamayā tatkṣaṇādeva apakrāntā || 59 ||

items.text: परित्यज्य तावप्युरणकौ गन्धर्वाः सुरलोकम् उपगताः ॥ ६० ॥
items.tr: parityajya tāvapyuraṇakau gandharvāḥ suralokam upagatāḥ || 60 ||

items.text: राजापि च तौ मेषावादाय अतिहृष्टमनाः स्वशयनमायातो नोर्वशीं ददर्श ॥ ६१ ॥
items.tr: rājāpi ca tau meṣāvādāya atihṛṣṭamanāḥ svaśayanamāyāto norvaśīṃ dadarśa || 61 ||

items.text: तां चापश्यन् व्यपगताम्बर एव उन्मत्तरूपो बभ्राम ॥ ६२ ॥
items.tr: tāṃ cāpaśyan vyapagatāmbara eva unmattarūpo babhrāma || 62 ||

items.text: कुरुक्षेत्रे च अम्भोजसरसि अन्याभिः चतसृभिः अप्सरोभिः समवेताम् उर्वशीं ददर्श ॥ ६३ ॥
items.tr: kurukṣetre ca ambhojasarasi anyābhiḥ catasṛbhiḥ apsarobhiḥ samavetām urvaśīṃ dadarśa || 63 ||

items.text: ततश्च उन्मत्तरूपो “जाये हे तिष्ठ, मनसि घोरे तिष्ठ, वचसि कपटिके तिष्ठ” इत्येवम् अनेकप्रकारं सूक्तमवोचत् ॥ ६४ ॥
items.tr: tataśca unmattarūpo “jāye he tiṣṭha, manasi ghore tiṣṭha, vacasi kapaṭike tiṣṭha” ityevam anekaprakāraṃ sūktamavocat || 64 ||

items.text: आह चोर्वशी ॥ ६५ ॥
items.tr: āha corvaśī || 65 ||

items.text: “महाराज अलमनेन अविवेकचेष्टितेन ॥ ६६ ॥
items.tr: “mahārāja alamanena avivekaceṣṭitena || 66 ||

items.text: अन्तर्वत्नी अहम् । अब्दान्ते भवतात्र आगन्तव्यम् । कुमारस्ते भविष्यति । एकां च निशामहं त्वया सह वत्स्यामि” इत्युक्तः प्रहृष्टः स्वपुरं जगाम ॥ ६७ ॥
items.tr: antarvatnī aham | abdānte bhavatātra āgantavyam | kumāraste bhaviṣyati | ekāṃ ca niśāmahaṃ tvayā saha vatsyāmi” ityuktaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ svapuraṃ jagāma || 67 ||

items.text: तासां चाप्सरसाम् उर्वशी कथयामास ॥ ६८ ॥
items.tr: tāsāṃ cāpsarasām urvaśī kathayāmāsa || 68 ||

items.text: “अयं स पुरुषोत्कृष्टो येन अहमेतावन्तं कालम् अनुरागाकृष्टमानसा सहोषिता” इति ॥ ६९ ॥
items.tr: “ayaṃ sa puruṣotkṛṣṭo yena ahametāvantaṃ kālam anurāgākṛṣṭamānasā sahoṣitā” iti || 69 ||

items.text: एवमुक्ताः ताः च अप्सरस ऊचुः ॥ ७० ॥
items.tr: evamuktāḥ tāḥ ca apsarasa ūcuḥ || 70 ||

items.text: “साधु साध्वस्य रूपम् । अप्यनेन सह अस्माकमपि सर्वकालमास्या भवेद्” इति ॥ ७१ ॥
items.tr: “sādhu sādhvasya rūpam | apyanena saha asmākamapi sarvakālamāsyā bhaved” iti || 71 ||

items.text: अब्दे च पूर्णे स राजा तत्राजगाम ॥ ७२ ॥
items.tr: abde ca pūrṇe sa rājā tatrājagāma || 72 ||

items.text: कुमारं च आयुषम् अस्मै च उर्वशी ददौ ॥ ७३ ॥
items.tr: kumāraṃ ca āyuṣam asmai ca urvaśī dadau || 73 ||

items.text: दत्त्वा चैकां निशां तेन राज्ञा सहोषित्वा, पञ्च पुत्रोत्पत्तये गर्भम् अवाप ॥ ७४ ॥
items.tr: dattvā caikāṃ niśāṃ tena rājñā sahoṣitvā, pañca putrotpattaye garbham avāpa || 74 ||

items.text: उवाच एनं राजानम् “अस्मत्प्रीत्या महाराजाय सर्व एव गन्धर्वा वरदाः संवृत्ताः । व्रियतां च वर” इति ॥ ७५ ॥
items.tr: uvāca enaṃ rājānam “asmatprītyā mahārājāya sarva eva gandharvā varadāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | vriyatāṃ ca vara” iti || 75 ||

items.text: आह च राजा ॥ ७६ ॥
items.tr: āha ca rājā || 76 ||

items.text: “विजितसकलारातिः अविहतेन्द्रियसामर्थ्यो बन्धुमान् अमितबलकोशोऽस्मि, नान्यदस्माकम् उर्वशीसालोक्यात् प्राप्तव्यमस्ति, तदहमनया सहोर्वश्या कालं नेतुम् अभिलषामि” इत्युक्ते गन्धर्वा राज्ञेऽग्निस्थालीं ददुः ॥ ७७ ॥
items.tr: “vijitasakalārātiḥ avihatendriyasāmarthyo bandhumān amitabalakośo'smi, nānyadasmākam urvaśīsālokyāt prāptavyamasti, tadahamanayā sahorvaśyā kālaṃ netum abhilaṣāmi” ityukte gandharvā rājñe'gnisthālīṃ daduḥ || 77 ||

items.text: ऊचुश्चैनम् “अग्निमाम्नायानुसारी भूत्वा, त्रिधा कृत्वा, उर्वशीसलोकतामनोरथम् उद्दिश्य सम्यग्यजेथाः । ततोऽवश्यम् अभिलषितम् अवाप्स्यति” इत्युक्तः तामग्निस्थालीम् आदाय जगाम ॥ ७८ ॥
items.tr: ūcuścainam “agnimāmnāyānusārī bhūtvā, tridhā kṛtvā, urvaśīsalokatāmanoratham uddiśya samyagyajethāḥ | tato'vaśyam abhilaṣitam avāpsyati” ityuktaḥ tāmagnisthālīm ādāya jagāma || 78 ||

items.text: अन्तरटव्याम् अचिन्तयत् “अहो मेऽतीव मूढता किमहम् अकरवम् ॥ ७९ ॥
items.tr: antaraṭavyām acintayat “aho me'tīva mūḍhatā kimaham akaravam || 79 ||

items.text: वह्निस्थाली मयैषा आनीता न उर्वशी” इति ॥ ८० ॥
items.tr: vahnisthālī mayaiṣā ānītā na urvaśī” iti || 80 ||

items.text: अथ एनाम् अटव्यामेव अग्निस्थालीं तत्याज स्वपुरं च जगाम ॥ ८१ ॥
items.tr: atha enām aṭavyāmeva agnisthālīṃ tatyāja svapuraṃ ca jagāma || 81 ||

items.text: व्यतीतेऽर्धरात्रे विनिद्रश्च अचिन्तयत् ॥ ८२ ॥
items.tr: vyatīte'rdharātre vinidraśca acintayat || 82 ||

items.text: “मम उर्वशीसालोक्यप्राप्त्यर्थम् अग्निस्थाली गन्धर्वैः दत्ता । सा च मया अटव्यां परित्यक्ता ॥ ८३ ॥
items.tr: “mama urvaśīsālokyaprāptyartham agnisthālī gandharvaiḥ dattā | sā ca mayā aṭavyāṃ parityaktā || 83 ||

items.text: तदहं तत्र तदाहरणाय यास्यामि” इत्युत्थाय तत्राप्युपगतो न अग्निस्थालीम् अपश्यत् ॥ ८४ ॥
items.tr: tadahaṃ tatra tadāharaṇāya yāsyāmi” ityutthāya tatrāpyupagato na agnisthālīm apaśyat || 84 ||

items.text: शमीगर्भं च अश्वत्थम् अग्निस्थालीस्थाने दृष्ट्वा अचिन्तयत् ॥ ८५ ॥
items.tr: śamīgarbhaṃ ca aśvattham agnisthālīsthāne dṛṣṭvā acintayat || 85 ||

items.text: “मयात्र अग्निस्थाली निक्षिप्ता सा च अश्वत्थः शमीगर्भोऽभूत् ॥ ८६ ॥
items.tr: “mayātra agnisthālī nikṣiptā sā ca aśvatthaḥ śamīgarbho'bhūt || 86 ||

items.text: तदेनमेव अहम् अग्निरूपमादाय, स्वपुरम् अभिगम्य, अरणीं कृत्वा, तदुत्पन्नाग्नेः उपास्तिं करिष्यामि” इति ॥ ८७ ॥
items.tr: tadenameva aham agnirūpamādāya, svapuram abhigamya, araṇīṃ kṛtvā, tadutpannāgneḥ upāstiṃ kariṣyāmi” iti || 87 ||

items.text: एवमेव स्वपुरमभिगम्य अरणिं चकार ॥ ८८ ॥
items.tr: evameva svapuramabhigamya araṇiṃ cakāra || 88 ||

items.text: तत्प्रमाणं चाङ्गुलैः कुर्वन् गायत्रीमपठत् ॥ ८९ ॥
items.tr: tatpramāṇaṃ cāṅgulaiḥ kurvan gāyatrīmapaṭhat || 89 ||

items.text: पठतश्च अक्षरसङ्ख्यानि एव अङ्गुलानि अरणी अभवत् ॥ ९० ॥
items.tr: paṭhataśca akṣarasaṅkhyāni eva aṅgulāni araṇī abhavat || 90 ||

items.text: तत्राग्निं निर्मथ्य, अग्नित्रयम् आम्नायानुसारी भूत्वा जुहाव ॥ ९१ ॥
items.tr: tatrāgniṃ nirmathya, agnitrayam āmnāyānusārī bhūtvā juhāva || 91 ||

items.text: उर्वशीसालोक्यं फलम् अभिसन्धितवान् ॥ ९२ ॥
items.tr: urvaśīsālokyaṃ phalam abhisandhitavān || 92 ||

items.text: तेनैव च अग्निविधिना बहुविधान् यज्ञान् इष्ट्वा, गान्धर्वलोकान् अवाप्य, उर्वश्या सह अवियोगम् अवाप ॥ ९३ ॥
items.tr: tenaiva ca agnividhinā bahuvidhān yajñān iṣṭvā, gāndharvalokān avāpya, urvaśyā saha aviyogam avāpa || 93 ||

items.text: एकोऽग्निः आदौ अभवत्, एकेन त्वत्र मन्वन्तरे त्रेधा प्रवर्तिताः ॥ ९४ ॥
items.tr: eko'gniḥ ādau abhavat, ekena tvatra manvantare tredhā pravartitāḥ || 94 ||

en_chapter: Maitreya said:—"O revered sir, you have described to me the solar dynasty but I wish to hear now of the kings of the lunar dynasty, who are still well-known for their glorious deeds. It behoves you to relate it gladly to me".

Parāçara said:—O foremost of Munis, hear from me, a description of the illustrious family of the moon which has produced many well-known kings of the earth. This family is adorned with many kings gifted with regal qualities of strength, valour, magnificence, prudence and energy such as Nahusha, Yayati, Kartavirya, Yaryuna and others. Hear I shall describe this family to you.

Atri was the son of Brahmā, the creator of the universe, who originated from the lotus that grew from the navel of Nārāyana. The son of Atri was Soma whom Brahmā made the king of plants, Brāhmans and of the stars. Some celebrated a Rajshuya sacrifice and on account of the glory derived therefrom and the vast sovereignty which he had acquired he grew haughty and licentious. He carried off Tārā, the wife of Vrihaspati, the preceptor of gods.

Soma did not give up Vrihaspati's wife though he was again and again requested by him, commanded by Brahmā and remonstrated by the holy sages. Usanas, who was an enemy of Vrihaspati, took the side of Soma. Rudra, who was a pupil of Angiras, the father of Vrihaspati, assisted his fellow student. Because their preceptor Usanas joined Soma, Jambha, Kujambha, all the Daityas, Dānavas and other enemies of the celestials came to his help. Indra and all other celestials assisted Vrihaspati.

Thus there took place a terrible combat which being on account of Tāraka was called Tarakāmaya or Tarakā war. In this the celestials led by Rudra hurled their weapons upon the Asuras and the Asuras equally overwhelmed the gods with weapons. Thus in the conflict between the gods and demons the universe, greatly overwhelmed, sought protection of Brahmā. Thereupon the glorious God asked Usanas with the demons and Rudra with the celestials to desist from fighting and give back Tārā to Vrihaspati. Finding that she was pregnant Vrihaspati desired her no longer to keep her burden and in satisfaction of his orders she was delivered of a son whom she kept in a clump of long Munja grass. And the child as soon as it was born proved its character of divinity by its radiance. Beholding both Vrihaspati and Soma fascinated by the beauty of the child the celestials, to know whose son it was, asked Tārā, saying "O damsel whose son is he? Is he Vrihaspati's or Soma's". Being thus addressed Tārā was ashamed and did not answer.

Though she was repeatedly asked by the celestials she was still mute and the child, being enraged, was about to curse her, saying—"Unless, O vile woman, you immediately speak out, who is my father, I shall so punish you for your useless shame that no woman in future shall speak the truth". Brahmā again interfered and pacifying the child said, addressing Tara "Tell me my daughter, is this the child of Vrihaspati or of Soma?" "Of Soma," said Tārā flushing. Thereupon the countenance of the king of constellations became bright, and expanded with joy. He at once embraced his son and said—"Well done my boy, forsooth thou art wise". And accordingly the boy was named Budha.

I have already described how Budha begot Pururavas on Ilā. Paruravas was a prince famous for liberality, devotion, magnificence, love of truth and beauty. Having incurred the curse of Mitra and Varuna, Urvasi made up her mind to live in the land of mortals and descending there saw Pururavas. As soon as a she saw him she forgot all reserve and not caring for the comforts to heaven became greatly attached to him. And finding her far superior to all other females in beauty, elegance, symmetry, and delicacy, Pururavas was equally enamoured of her. Both the man and the woman were equally attached to each other and thought no more of any other object. The king then boldly said—"Fair woman, I love you; have pity on me and return my affection". Urvasi turning her face a little through modesty said—"I will do so, if you satisfy the conditions I propose to you".

"What are they?" asked the king "speak them out". "I have two rams" said the nymph "which I love like my children; they must be kept by my bed-side and shall not be allowed to be carried away. You must not be seen by me undressed and clarified butter alone shall be my food". The king readily agreed to these terms.

After this Pururavas and Urvasi lived together for sixty one thousand years in Alakā, sporting amidst the groves and lakes of Chaitraratha abounding in lotuses and the other forests. By these enjoyments Urvasi's attachment increased every day and she forgot all desire for residing in the region of immortals. In the absence of Urvasi heaven appeared devoid of beauty to the celestials, nymphs, genii and quiristers. Knowing the engagement that Urvasi had contracted with the king, Viswasvasu was appointed by the Gandharvas to bring about its dissolution. And coming by night to the room where they were sleeping he carried off one of the rams: Urvasi got up by its cries and exclaimed—"Ah me! who has stolen one of my children: Had I got a husband this would not have taken place. To whom shall I go for help?" The king heard the lamentations but could not go lest he might be seen undressed. The Gandharvas then took away another ram. Again hearing the sound of its being stolen away in the sky she lamented saying—"Alas I have got no husband. I have taken the shelter of a dastardly person". Thinking "it is darkness" the king took up a dagger and pursued them, saying—"stop, O wicked I shall soon slay you". Immediately the Gandharvas created a flash of brilliant lightning in the room and the king was seen undressed by Urvasi. The contract was broken and she instantly disappeared. And leaving behind the rams the Gandharvas too went to the region of the celestials. Taking the rams, the king, delighted came back to his bed-room but found no Urvasi. Not finding her he wandered naked all over the world like a maniac. At length arriving at Kurukshetra he saw Urvasi sporting with four other nymphs in a lake abounding in lotuses. Like a mad man the king neared him and exclaimed—"O my wife, wait, speak with me, O thou of an iron heart". Urvasi replied—"O great king useless is this inconsiderate attempt. I am now pregnant, go away just now and come here again after a year when I shall give you a son and remain with you for one night". Being thus solaced Pururavas came back to his capital. Urvasi then said to her mates. "This king is that excellent man bring drawn by whose attachment I lived for such a long time". Hearing this the other nymphs said, "Great is his beauty; we too with him could live happily for ever".

After the expiration of a year the king again came to that place and Urvasi gave him a son by the name of Ayus. Living with him for one night she again became pregnant to bear to him five sons. She then said to the king—"O king all the Gandharvas, on account of their regard for me, are ready to confer upon thee a boon. Do thou pray for it". The king said—"I have slain all my enemies—my faculties are all very powerful; I have friends, relations, armies and treasures; so there is nothing which I want but living with my Urvasi in the same region. So I wish to live with her always".

After he had spoken this the Gandharvas brought to him a vessel with fire and said,—"Take this fire and according to the precepts of the Vedas divide it into three parts: then offer oblation to it for Urvasi and your desires shall thus be gratified". The Gandharvas having said this, the king took the vessel and went away. Then coming to a forest he thought—"Oh, what stupid I am; I have brought this vessel but not Urvasi". Then leaving the vessel there he came back to his capital. When half the night had passed he awoke and thought—"The Gandharvas conferred upon me this vessel of fire to enable me to live with Urvasi. I have left that in the forest. I shall go there to bring it". Having said this he went there but did not find the vessel. Then beholding a young Ashwattha tree growing out of a Sami plant he argued within himself—"I left here a vessel of fire and I now see a young Ashwattha tree growing out of a Sami plant. I shall take this type of fire to my capital and having created fire by their attrition I will worship it".

Having thus made up his mind he took the plants to his city and made their wood for attrition with pieces of as many inches as there are syllables in the Gayatri. He recited that verse and rubbed together sticks of as many inches as he recited syllables in the Gayatri, Having created fire there-from he divided it into three portions according to the precepts of the Vedas and offered oblations to it with the view of obtaining re-union with Urvasi. Having performed many sacrifices with this fire he attained to the region of the Gandharvas and suffered no more separation from his beloved Urvasi. Thus fire, that was at first one, was made three-fold in the present Manwantara by the son of Ilā.
